title: The helpful util
context: A developer asked an AI assistant to check whether a config file exists before reading it, using Node's promise-based fs module. The suggestion crashes on every single call, even when the file is present.
question: What's wrong with this function?
options: fs/promises has no exists method — Node's promise-based fs API never shipped one.
JSON.parse is called before readFile's promise resolves.
readFile should be called with a Buffer encoding instead of 'utf-8'.
The function needs to validate that path is a string before use.

explanation.theBug: fs/promises does not export an exists function. The synchronous and callback-based fs module has existsSync and a deprecated callback fs.exists, but the promises API deliberately omits an exists check — Node's own docs recommend fs.access or a try/catch around readFile instead. Calling fs.exists here throws TypeError: fs.exists is not a function.
explanation.whyAIGeneratesThis: Every other method in fs/promises mirrors its callback-based counterpart (readFile, writeFile, mkdir), so the model extrapolates that exists must follow the same pattern — even though Node's maintainers specifically chose not to promisify exists, because of a well-known time-of-check-to-time-of-use race condition it tends to encourage.

theFix.commentary: Prefer attempting the read and handling ENOENT over a separate existence check — it also avoids the race between checking and reading.

explanation.reviewHeuristic: Don't assume every callback-style Node API has a matching promise-based twin — check the fs/promises docs before relying on a method name.
